elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Section 14 expressly permits Client to terminate the Agreement for convenience at any time.

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: Termination may occur “upon written notice,” with no advance-notice period required; the separate service wind-down does not impose more than 30 days' advance notice to exercise termination.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: The rendered language contains no pro-rata refund obligation for prepaid fees.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: TrueLink is given only an end-of-term non-renewal right on 90 days' notice, not a convenience-termination right during the one-year term.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Client may terminate upon written notice without a 60-to-90-day advance-notice requirement. The service wind-down timing is not such a termination notice period.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee is imposed, so the conditional cap requirement is satisfied.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: TrueLink's only convenience-like exit right is non-renewal effective at the end of the applicable one-year term.

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: TrueLink must give written notice of non-renewal no later than 90 days before the end of the year.
